summary: Two neighbouring $^{28}$Si/SiGe micromagnet spin qubits are compared, one sitting at a sweet spot where the longitudinal field gradient is locally minimized. At the sweet spot $T_2^*$ reaches 67 µs and CPMG coherence 4.6 ms versus $T_2^* = 5.2$ µs next door, with residual noise consistent with $^{29}$Si nuclear spins at 800 ppm.
motivation: Micromagnet gradients convert charge noise into qubit frequency noise, which limits spin-qubit coherence.
method: They measure coherence times, frequency-noise power spectra and inter-qubit noise correlations for a sweet-spot qubit and a large-gradient neighbour in the same device.
result: Frequency noise near 1 Hz is almost two orders of magnitude lower at the sweet spot, and the weakly correlated residual spectrum matches the prediction for $^{29}$Si nuclear-spin noise.
